𝐁𝐨𝐲𝐳 𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐇𝐨𝐨𝐝, 𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟏.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Most movies about life in the hoods of Los Angeles, New York City, and other urban areas of the U.S. are discounted as novelty entertainment for audiences seeking a thrill. Out of an era of gangster rap came a nationwide exposure of the issues within the Black and Latino communities, and directors like John Singleton and the Hughes Brothers follow in the footsteps of the great Spike Lee.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
This movie is an intricate examination of the archetypes and stereotypes of the hood, as well as an introduction to the survivors, both trapped in the violence and escaping the cycle. 𝐁𝐨𝐲𝐬 𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐇𝐨𝐨𝐝 (𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟏) concentrates on a Black community without the interactions between communities shown in 𝘋𝘰 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘙𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘛𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 (𝟷𝟿𝟾𝟿), another epic race commentary. The message here is deeper than White or Italian based gangland movies, because the human aspect and the characters are more solid and approachable, and rooted in highly intellectual and applicable theories on race and violence. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
This movie is a showcase of the radical and moderate themes expressed by Black activists, with Laurence Fishburne’s character as the leader and role model of the film. Don’t underestimate the power of this film. A must watch.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Rate this one out of ten. 👀 🔟
